"""Application service for controlled Announcement Operations lifecycle."""
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from backend.app.domain.announcements.announcement import Announcement
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_event import PublicationEvent, PublicationEventType
from .announcement_repository import AnnouncementRepository
from .publication_event_repository import PublicationEventRepository


class AnnouncementOperationsService:
    """Coordinates lifecycle changes and immutable audit events.

    This foundation intentionally does not deliver to Telegram. Delivery is a
    later adapter behind an explicit port so the domain remains provider-independent.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, repository: AnnouncementRepository, event_repository: PublicationEventRepository) -> None:
        self._repository = repository
        self._events = event_repository

    async def create(self, *, title: str, body: str, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        if not title.strip() or not body.strip() or not actor.strip():
            raise ValueError("title, body and actor are required.")
        announcement = Announcement(title=title.strip(), body=body.strip(), created_by=actor.strip())
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.CREATED, actor, correlation_id)
        return announcement

    async def mark_ready_for_review(self, announcement_id: UUID, *, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._require(announcement_id)
        announcement.mark_ready_for_review()
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.READY_FOR_REVIEW, actor, correlation_id)
        return announcement

    async def approve(self, announcement_id: UUID, *, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._require(announcement_id)
        announcement.approve(actor)
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.APPROVED, actor, correlation_id)
        return announcement

    async def request_publication(self, announcement_id: UUID, *, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._require(announcement_id)
        announcement.request_publication()
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.PUBLISH_REQUESTED, actor, correlation_id)
        return announcement

    async def mark_published(self, announcement_id: UUID, *, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None = None, provider_message_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._require(announcement_id)
        announcement.mark_published()
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.PUBLISHED, actor, correlation_id, provider_message_id=provider_message_id)
        return announcement

    async def mark_failed(self, announcement_id: UUID, *, actor: str, error_code: str, correlation_id: str | None = None) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._require(announcement_id)
        announcement.mark_failed()
        await self._repository.save(announcement)
        await self._audit(announcement, PublicationEventType.FAILED, actor, correlation_id, error_code=error_code)
        return announcement

    async def get(self, announcement_id: UUID) -> Announcement:
        return await self._require(announcement_id)

    async def list(self) -> tuple[Announcement, ...]:
        return await self._repository.list()

    async def audit_log(self, announcement_id: UUID) -> tuple[PublicationEvent, ...]:
        await self._require(announcement_id)
        return await self._events.list_for_publication(announcement_id)

    async def _require(self, announcement_id: UUID) -> Announcement:
        announcement = await self._repository.get(announcement_id)
        if announcement is None:
            raise LookupError(f"Announcement {announcement_id} was not found.")
        return announcement

    async def _audit(self, announcement: Announcement, event_type: PublicationEventType, actor: str, correlation_id: str | None, *, error_code: str | None = None, provider_message_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        if not actor.strip():
            raise ValueError("actor cannot be empty.")
        await self._events.append(PublicationEvent(
            publication_id=announcement.id,
            event_type=event_type,
            actor=actor,
            correlation_id=correlation_id or str(uuid4()),
            error_code=error_code,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        ))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from enum import Enum


class AnnouncementAuditEventType(str, Enum):
    CREATED = "created"
    APPROVAL_REQUESTED = "approval_requested"
    APPROVED = "approved"
    PUBLISH_STARTED = "publish_started"
    PUBLISHED = "published"
    PUBLISH_FAILED = "publish_failed"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AnnouncementAuditEvent:
    publication_id: str
    event_type: AnnouncementAuditEventType
    occurred_at: datetime
    details: str | None = None


class InMemoryAnnouncementAuditSink:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._events: list[AnnouncementAuditEvent] = []

    def record(
        self,
        publication_id: str,
        event_type: AnnouncementAuditEventType,
        details: str | None = None,
    ) -> AnnouncementAuditEvent:
        event = AnnouncementAuditEvent(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            event_type=event_type,
            occurred_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            details=details,
        )
        self._events.append(event)
        return event

    def list_for(self, publication_id: str) -> tuple[AnnouncementAuditEvent, ...]:
        return tuple(e for e in self._events if e.publication_id == publication_id)

"""Small deterministic repositories for tests and local foundation work."""
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from backend.app.domain.announcements.announcement import Announcement
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication_event import PublicationEvent


class InMemoryAnnouncementRepository:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[UUID, Announcement] = {}

    async def save(self, announcement: Announcement) -> Announcement:
        self._items[announcement.id] = announcement
        return announcement

    async def get(self, announcement_id: UUID) -> Announcement | None:
        return self._items.get(announcement_id)

    async def list(self) -> tuple[Announcement, ...]:
        return tuple(self._items.values())


class InMemoryPublicationEventRepository:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._events: list[PublicationEvent] = []

    async def append(self, event: PublicationEvent) -> PublicationEvent:
        self._events.append(event)
        return event

    async def list_for_publication(self, publication_id: UUID) -> tuple[PublicationEvent, ...]:
        return tuple(e for e in self._events if e.publication_id == publication_id)

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Mapping

from backend.app.application.announcements.repositories import PublicationRepository
from backend.app.application.announcements.template_registry import AnnouncementTemplateRegistry
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication import Publication
from backend.app.domain.announcements.template_models import PublicationStatus


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PublicationPreview:
    publication_type: str
    template_id: str
    template_version: int
    content: str


class AnnouncementPublicationService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        templates: AnnouncementTemplateRegistry,
        publications: PublicationRepository,
    ) -> None:
        if templates is None or publications is None:
            raise ValueError("templates and publications are required.")
        self._templates = templates
        self._publications = publications

    def preview(
        self,
        *,
        template_id: str,
        values: Mapping[str, str],
        version: int | None = None,
    ) -> PublicationPreview:
        template = self._templates.get_version(template_id, version)
        content = self._templates.preview(
            template_id=template_id,
            values=dict(values),
            version=template.version,
        )
        return PublicationPreview(
            publication_type=template.publication_type.value,
            template_id=template.template_id,
            template_version=template.version,
            content=content,
        )

    def create(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: str,
        template_id: str,
        title: str,
        values: Mapping[str, str],
        version: int | None = None,
    ) -> Publication:
        template = self._templates.get_version(template_id, version)
        content = self._templates.preview(
            template_id=template_id,
            values=dict(values),
            version=template.version,
        )
        publication = Publication(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            template_id=template.template_id,
            template_version=template.version,
            publication_type=template.publication_type,
            title=title,
            content=content,
            status=PublicationStatus.DRAFT,
        )
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

    def _get(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._publications.get(publication_id)
        if publication is None:
            raise LookupError(f"Unknown publication '{publication_id}'.")
        return publication

    def request_approval(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._get(publication_id)
        publication.request_approval()
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

    def approve(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._get(publication_id)
        publication.approve()
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

    def begin_publish(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._get(publication_id)
        publication.begin_publish()
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

    def mark_publish_failure(self, publication_id: str, reason: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._get(publication_id)
        publication.mark_failure(reason)
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

    def mark_publish_success(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication:
        publication = self._get(publication_id)
        publication.publish_success()
        self._publications.save(publication)
        return publication

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Mapping


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEditorField:
    """UI-safe representation of one template input."""

    name: str
    required: bool
    label: str
    multiline: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEditorOption:
    """UI-safe approved template option."""

    template_id: str
    name: str
    category: str
    description: str
    version: int
    publication_type: str
    fields: tuple[TemplateEditorField, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEditorPreview:
    """Preview result returned without creating or publishing a publication."""

    template_id: str
    template_version: int
    publication_type: str
    content: str


def field_label(name: str) -> str:
    """Convert a controlled field identifier into an operator-friendly label."""
    return name.replace("_", " ").strip().title()


def is_multiline_field(name: str) -> bool:
    """Keep long-form announcement fields in a textarea."""
    return name.lower() in {
        "body",
        "content",
        "summary",
        "description",
        "details",
        "message",
        "changes",
    }


def build_editor_fields(
    required_fields: frozenset[str],
    optional_fields: frozenset[str],
) -> tuple[TemplateEditorField, ...]:
    names = sorted(set(required_fields) | set(optional_fields))
    required = set(required_fields)

    return tuple(
        TemplateEditorField(
            name=name,
            required=name in required,
            label=field_label(name),
            multiline=is_multiline_field(name),
        )
        for name in names

class AnnouncementTemplateEditorService:
    """Application service for the template-driven publication editor.

    This service only prepares editor metadata, validates/preview-renders
    template values, and creates drafts. It has no channel/provider dependency
    and never performs external publication.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        templates: AnnouncementTemplateRegistry,
        publications: AnnouncementPublicationService,
    ) -> None:
        if templates is None or publications is None:
            raise ValueError("templates and publications are required.")
        self._templates = templates
        self._publications = publications

    def list_approved_templates(self) -> tuple[TemplateEditorOption, ...]:
        template_models = self._templates.list_templates()

        return tuple(
            TemplateEditorOption(
                template_id=template.template_id,
                name=template.name,
                category=(
                    template.category
                    if template.category
                    else template.publication_type.value
                ),
                description=template.description
                or "Approved announcement pattern.",
                version=template.active_version,
                publication_type=template.publication_type.value,
                fields=build_editor_fields(
                    template.get_version().required_fields,
                    template.get_version().optional_fields,
                ),
            )
            for template in template_models
        )

    def preview(
        self,
        *,
        template_id: str,
        values: Mapping[str, str],
        version: int | None = None,
    ) -> TemplateEditorPreview:
        result = self._publications.preview(
            template_id=template_id,
            values=values,
            version=version,
        )
        return TemplateEditorPreview(
            template_id=result.template_id,
            template_version=result.template_version,
            publication_type=result.publication_type,
            content=result.content,
        )

    def create_draft(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: str,
        template_id: str,
        title: str,
        values: Mapping[str, str],
        version: int | None = None,
    ):
        return self._publications.create(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            template_id=template_id,
            title=title,
            values=values,
            version=version,
        )

from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.application.announcements.repositories import AnnouncementTemplateRepository
from backend.app.domain.announcements.template_models import (
    AnnouncementTemplate,
    AnnouncementTemplateVersion,
    render_template,
)


class AnnouncementTemplateRegistry:
    def __init__(self, repository: AnnouncementTemplateRepository) -> None:
        if repository is None:
            raise ValueError("repository cannot be None.")
        self._repository = repository

    def register(self, template: AnnouncementTemplate) -> None:
        if self._repository.get(template.template_id) is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"Template '{template.template_id}' already exists.")
        self._repository.save(template)

    def list_templates(self) -> tuple[AnnouncementTemplate, ...]:
        """Return the approved template catalog in deterministic order."""
        return tuple(
            sorted(
                self._repository.list_all(),
                key=lambda item: (item.name.lower(), item.template_id),
            )
        )

    def get_version(
        self,
        template_id: str,
        version: int | None = None,
    ) -> AnnouncementTemplateVersion:
        template = self._repository.get(template_id)
        if template is None:
            raise LookupError(f"Unknown template '{template_id}'.")
        return template.get_version(version)

    def preview(
        self,
        *,
        template_id: str,
        values: dict[str, str],
        version: int | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        return render_template(self.get_version(template_id, version), values)

class AnnouncementPublicationApprovalService:
    """Authorized application boundary for WS-23.1.3 approval.

    Lifecycle validation remains in the Publication domain model.
    Persistence remains behind PublicationRepository.
    Telegram delivery is deliberately outside this service.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publications: AnnouncementPublicationService,
        audit: PublicationApprovalAudit,
    ) -> None:
        if publications is None or audit is None:
            raise ValueError("publications and audit are required.")
        self._publications = publications
        self._audit = audit

    async def approve(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: str,
        actor: str,
    ) -> PublicationApprovalResult:

            raise ValueError("actor cannot be empty.")

        publication = self._publications.approve(publication_id)

            publication=publication,
            actor=actor.strip(),
            occurred_at=approved_at,

            publication=publication,

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Protocol

from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication import Publication
from backend.app.domain.announcements.template_models import PublicationStatus


class AsyncPublicationStore(Protocol):
    async def get_async(self, publication_id: str) -> Publication | None:
        ...

    async def save_async(self, publication: Publication) -> None:
        ...


class PublicationApprovalAudit(Protocol):
    async def record_approval(
        self,
        *,
        publication: Publication,
        actor: str,
        occurred_at: datetime,
    ) -> None:
        ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AsyncPublicationApprovalResult:
    publication: Publication
    actor: str
    approved_at: datetime


class AsyncAnnouncementPublicationApprovalService:
    """Async PostgreSQL-backed approval application boundary.

    The domain model remains the authority for lifecycle transitions.
    This service never invokes WS-22 execution or Telegram.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publications: AsyncPublicationStore,
        audit: PublicationApprovalAudit,
    ) -> None:
        if publications is None or audit is None:
            raise ValueError("publications and audit are required.")
        self._publications = publications
        self._audit = audit

    async def approve(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: str,
        actor: str,
    ) -> AsyncPublicationApprovalResult:
        if not actor.strip():
            raise ValueError("actor cannot be empty.")

        publication = await self._publications.get_async(publication_id)
        if publication is None:
            raise LookupError(f"Unknown publication '{publication_id}'.")

        if publication.status is not PublicationStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL:
            # Use the domain transition so the canonical lifecycle error remains
            # authoritative and consistent with the existing domain model.
            publication.approve()

        else:
            publication.approve()

        approved_at = publication.approved_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        await self._publications.save_async(publication)
        await self._audit.record_approval(
            publication=publication,
            actor=actor.strip(),
            occurred_at=approved_at,
        )

        return AsyncPublicationApprovalResult(
            publication=publication,
            actor=actor.strip(),
            approved_at=approved_at,
        )


__all__ = [
    "AsyncAnnouncementPublicationApprovalService",
    "AsyncPublicationApprovalResult",

    admin_authorizer: AdminAuthorizer,

    """
    Compose the WS-23.1.3 approval boundary.

    The composition root owns dependency creation.

    This function:
    - reuses the injected approval service;
    - reuses the injected administrator authorizer;
    - creates only the API router;

        approval_service=approval_service,

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import UUID

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionResult,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_execution_service import (
    DurablePublicationExecutionService,
)
from backend.app.domain.announcements.publication import Publication


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ApprovedPublicationExecutionService:
    """Application boundary from WS-23 approved state into WS-22."""

    durable_execution: DurablePublicationExecutionService

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.durable_execution is None:
            raise ValueError("durable_execution cannot be None.")

    async def execute(
        self,
        *,
        publication: Publication,
        actor: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
        correlation_id: str,
    ) -> PublicationExecutionResult:
        """Delegate an approved publication to the existing WS-22 service.

        WS-22 remains responsible for:
        - durable execution;
        - idempotency;
        - execution persistence;
        - execution audit;
        - retry semantics;
        - controlled provider invocation.
        """

        if publication is None:
            raise ValueError("publication cannot be None.")

        if not actor.strip():
            raise ValueError("actor cannot be empty.")

        if not idempotency_key.strip():
            raise ValueError("idempotency_key cannot be empty.")

        if not correlation_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("correlation_id cannot be empty.")

        try:
            publication_uuid = UUID(publication.publication_id)
        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise ValueError(
                "Approved publication ID must be a UUID for WS-22 durable execution."
            ) from exc

        request = PublicationExecutionRequest(
            publication_id=publication_uuid,
            idempotency_key=idempotency_key.strip(),
            correlation_id=correlation_id.strip(),
            actor=actor.strip(),
        )

        return await self.durable_execution.execute(
            publication=_PublicationExecutionAdapter(publication),
            request=request,
        )


class _PublicationExecutionAdapter:
    """Adapt the WS-23 publication to the existing WS-22 execution contract."""

    def __init__(self, publication: Publication) -> None:
        self._publication = publication

    @property
    def id(self) -> UUID:
        return UUID(self._publication.publication_id)

    @property
    def title(self) -> str:
        return self._publication.title

    @property
    def content(self) -> str:
        return self._publication.content

    @property
    def status(self):
        return self._publication.status

    def begin_publish(self) -> None:
        self._publication.begin_publish()

    def mark_failure(self, reason: str) -> None:
        self._publication.mark_failure(reason)

    def publish_success(self, provider_message_id: str | None = None) -> None:
        del provider_message_id
        self._publication.publish_success()


__all__ = ["ApprovedPublicationExecutionService"]

"""WS-22.3.4 execution audit adapters.

WS-22.3.4.1:
    PublicationExecutionAuditAdapter
    Bridges the execution audit contract to the existing in-memory
    announcement audit vocabulary.

WS-22.3.4.2:
    DurablePublicationExecutionAudit
    Bridges the same execution contract to the durable audit repository.

Both implementations intentionally share the same execution-facing
contract. They differ only in persistence destination.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from backend.app.application.announcements.audit import (
    AnnouncementAuditEventType,
    InMemoryAnnouncementAuditSink,
)


class PublicationExecutionAuditAdapter:
    """WS-22.3.4.1 adapter for the existing announcement audit sink."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        sink: InMemoryAnnouncementAuditSink,
    ) -> None:
        if sink is None:
            raise ValueError("sink cannot be None.")

        self._sink = sink

    async def record_success(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        provider_message_id: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        self._sink.record(
            publication_id=str(publication_id),
            event_type=AnnouncementAuditEventType.PUBLISHED,
            details=(
                f"actor={actor};"
                f"correlation_id={correlation_id};"
                f"provider_message_id={provider_message_id}"
            ),
        )

    async def record_failure(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        error_code: str,
    ) -> None:
        self._sink.record(
            publication_id=str(publication_id),
            event_type=AnnouncementAuditEventType.PUBLISH_FAILED,
            details=(
                f"actor={actor};"
                f"correlation_id={correlation_id};"
                f"error_code={error_code}"
            ),
        )


class DurablePublicationExecutionAudit:
    """WS-22.3.4.2 adapter for the durable audit repository."""

    def __init__(self, *, repository) -> None:
        if repository is None:
            raise ValueError("repository cannot be None.")

        self._repository = repository

    async def record_success(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        provider_message_id: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        await self._repository.record_success(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            actor=actor,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )

    async def record_failure(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        error_code: str,
    ) -> None:
        await self._repository.record_failure(
            publication_id=publication_id,
            actor=actor,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            error_code=error_code,
        )

"""WS-22.3.5.3 canonical durable publication execution composition.

This module is the composition boundary for the WS-22 durable execution
vertical slice.

It deliberately does not create a new persistence architecture. The
canonical PostgreSQL engine and async session factory are supplied by the
platform persistence boundary in:

    backend.app.infrastructure.persistence.database

The resulting object graph is:

    PostgreSQL
        |
        v
    canonical async session factory
        |
        +--> execution repository
        |
        +--> audit repository
                  |
                  v
        DurablePublicationExecutionAudit
                  |
                  v
        DurablePublicationExecutionService

Provider selection remains outside this module.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.audit_adapter import (
    DurablePublicationExecutionAudit,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_execution_service import (
    DurablePublicationExecutionService,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.announcements.publication_audit_repository import (
    SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.announcements.sqlalchemy_publication_execution_repository import (
    SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository,
)
from backend.app.infrastructure.persistence.database import (
    create_async_database_engine,
    create_async_session_factory,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DurablePublicationExecutionComposition:
    """Fully composed WS-22 durable execution boundary."""

    engine: AsyncEngine
    session_factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
    execution_repository: SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository
    audit_repository: SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository
    audit: DurablePublicationExecutionAudit
    service: DurablePublicationExecutionService

    async def dispose(self) -> None:
        """Release the shared PostgreSQL async engine."""

        await self.engine.dispose()


def create_durable_publication_execution_composition(
    *,
    publisher,
) -> DurablePublicationExecutionComposition:
    """Create the canonical WS-22 durable execution graph.

    The publisher is deliberately injected because provider selection belongs
    outside the durable execution composition.

    This function creates exactly one PostgreSQL engine and exactly one async
    session factory. Both durable repositories receive that same factory.
    """

    if publisher is None:
        raise ValueError("publisher cannot be None.")

    engine = create_async_database_engine()
    session_factory = create_async_session_factory(engine)

    execution_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationExecutionRepository(
        session_factory
    )

    audit_repository = SqlAlchemyPublicationAuditRepository(
        session_factory
    )

    audit = DurablePublicationExecutionAudit(
        repository=audit_repository,
    )

    service = DurablePublicationExecutionService(
        publisher=publisher,
        execution_repository=execution_repository,
        audit=audit,
    )

    return DurablePublicationExecutionComposition(
        engine=engine,
        session_factory=session_factory,
        execution_repository=execution_repository,
        audit_repository=audit_repository,
        audit=audit,
        service=service,
    )


__all__ = [
    "DurablePublicationExecutionComposition",
    "create_durable_publication_execution_composition",
]

from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    AnnouncementPublisher,
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionResult,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)
from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.durable_contracts import (
    DurableExecutionStatus,
    PublicationExecutionRepository,
)


class DurablePublicationExecutionService:
    """Retry-safe execution service backed by durable idempotency state.

    A completed idempotency key is never sent again.

    A STARTED record is treated as an interrupted attempt and is retryable.

    A FAILED record is also retryable. Before a retry is executed, the
    repository is responsible for incrementing the durable attempt counter
    and transitioning the record back to STARTED.

    The repository implementation must make creation atomic against a
    unique idempotency key.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publisher: AnnouncementPublisher,
        execution_repository: PublicationExecutionRepository,
        audit,
    ) -> None:
        if publisher is None:
            raise ValueError("publisher cannot be None.")

        if execution_repository is None:
            raise ValueError("execution_repository cannot be None.")

        if audit is None:
            raise ValueError("audit cannot be None.")

        self._publisher = publisher
        self._repository = execution_repository
        self._audit = audit

    async def execute(
        self,
        *,
        publication,
        request: PublicationExecutionRequest,
    ) -> PublicationExecutionResult:
        existing = await self._repository.get_by_idempotency_key(
            request.idempotency_key
        )

        # A successful execution is terminal for the idempotency key.
        # Never call the external provider again.
        if (
            existing is not None
            and existing.status is DurableExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
        ):
            return PublicationExecutionResult(
                publication_id=existing.publication_id,
                status=PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY,
                idempotency_key=existing.idempotency_key,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                provider_message_id=existing.provider_message_id,
            )

        self._assert_approved(publication)

        # The repository owns the atomic unique-key operation. If another
        # worker already created the same key, re-read and honour its state.
        if existing is None:
            try:
                record = await self._repository.create_started(
                    publication_id=publication.id,
                    idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
                    correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                )
            except Exception:
                record = await self._repository.get_by_idempotency_key(
                    request.idempotency_key
                )

                if record is None:
                    raise

        elif existing.status is DurableExecutionStatus.FAILED:
            # A FAILED execution is retryable. Reuse the same durable
            # idempotency record and increment its attempt number rather
            # than creating a second row.
            record = await self._repository.start_retry(
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            )

        else:
            # STARTED represents an interrupted/incomplete attempt.
            # Preserve the existing durable attempt number and retry it.
            record = existing

        publication.begin_publish()

        try:
            provider_message_id = await self._publisher.publish(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                title=publication.title,
                content=publication.content,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            error_code = self._error_code(exc)

            publication.mark_failure(error_code)

            await self._repository.mark_failed(
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
                error_code=error_code,
            )

            await self._audit.record_failure(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                actor=request.actor,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                error_code=error_code,
            )

            return PublicationExecutionResult(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                status=PublicationExecutionStatus.FAILED,
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                error_code=error_code,
            )

        publication.publish_success(provider_message_id)

        await self._repository.mark_succeeded(
            idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )

        await self._audit.record_success(
            publication_id=publication.id,
            actor=request.actor,
            correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )

        return PublicationExecutionResult(
            publication_id=publication.id,
            status=PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
            idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _assert_approved(publication) -> None:
        value = getattr(publication.status, "value", publication.status)

        if value != "approved":
            raise ValueError(
                "Only approved publications may be executed."
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _error_code(exc: Exception) -> str:
        explicit = getattr(exc, "error_code", None)

        return (
            explicit.strip()[:100]
            if isinstance(explicit, str) and explicit.strip()
            else type(exc).__name__.upper()[:100]
        )

"""WS-22.3.3.x legacy publisher migration bridge.

This module provides the explicit migration boundary between the existing
Beta announcement publisher contract and the canonical WS-22 execution
publisher contract.

The bridge is intentionally provider-independent. It does not know about
Telegram, HTTP, credentials, or external SDKs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol
from uuid import UUID

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    AnnouncementPublisher,
)


class LegacyAnnouncementPublisher(Protocol):
    """Existing Beta publisher contract.

    This protocol mirrors the legacy application boundary that is still used
    by the existing ControlledAnnouncementPublisher path.

    It is intentionally isolated here as a migration dependency and must not
    be used by the new WS-22 execution service.
    """

    async def publish(
        self,
        *,
        channel_id: str,
        text: str,
    ) -> str:
        """Publish using the existing legacy publication boundary."""


class LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge(AnnouncementPublisher):
    """Adapt the existing publisher to the canonical WS-22 port.

    The bridge is the temporary migration boundary between:

        WS-22 execution contract
                    â†“
        legacy announcement publisher
                    â†“
        existing provider adapter

    No provider-specific behaviour belongs here.

    The channel identifier is configuration supplied by the composition root.
    It is deliberately not persisted or invented by the execution service.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publisher: LegacyAnnouncementPublisher,
        channel_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        if publisher is None:
            raise ValueError("publisher cannot be None.")

        if not channel_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("channel_id cannot be empty.")

        self._publisher = publisher
        self._channel_id = channel_id

    async def publish(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        title: str,
        content: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
    ) -> str | None:
        """Publish through the existing legacy publisher.

        WS-22 execution metadata is deliberately not passed to the legacy
        publisher because that older contract does not support it.

        Idempotency and correlation remain owned by the WS-22 execution
        service and durable execution repository.
        """

        del publication_id
        del correlation_id
        del idempotency_key

        text = self._compose_message(
            title=title,
            content=content,
        )

        return await self._publisher.publish(
            channel_id=self._channel_id,
            text=text,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _compose_message(
        *,
        title: str,
        content: str,
    ) -> str:
        normalized_title = title.strip()
        normalized_content = content.strip()

        if not normalized_title:
            raise ValueError("title cannot be empty.")

        if not normalized_content:
            raise ValueError("content cannot be empty.")

        return f"{normalized_title}\n\n{normalized_content}"


__all__ = [
    "LegacyAnnouncementPublisher",
    "LegacyAnnouncementPublisherBridge",
]

"""WS-22.3.1 provider-independent publication execution service."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol
from uuid import UUID

from backend.app.application.announcements.execution.contracts import (
    AnnouncementPublisher,
    PublicationExecutionRequest,
    PublicationExecutionResult,
    PublicationExecutionStatus,
)


class ExecutablePublication(Protocol):
    """Minimum aggregate surface required by the execution service."""

    id: UUID
    title: str
    content: str
    status: object

    def begin_publish(self) -> None: ...

    def publish_success(self, provider_message_id: str | None = None) -> None: ...

    def mark_failure(self, reason: str) -> None: ...


class PublicationExecutionAudit(Protocol):
    """Minimal audit boundary used by execution.

    The concrete publication-event repository remains an existing
    application concern; this protocol prevents execution from coupling to
    a particular persistence implementation.
    """

    async def record_success(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        provider_message_id: str | None,
    ) -> None: ...

    async def record_failure(
        self,
        *,
        publication_id: UUID,
        actor: str,
        correlation_id: str,
        error_code: str,
    ) -> None: ...


class PublicationExecutionService:
    """Execute approved publications through a provider-independent port.

    The service owns orchestration and idempotency. It does not know which
    channel/provider performs the external publication.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publisher: AnnouncementPublisher,
        audit: PublicationExecutionAudit,
    ) -> None:
        if publisher is None:
            raise ValueError("publisher cannot be None.")
        if audit is None:
            raise ValueError("audit cannot be None.")
        self._publisher = publisher
        self._audit = audit
        self._completed: dict[str, PublicationExecutionResult] = {}

    async def execute(
        self,
        *,
        publication: ExecutablePublication,
        request: PublicationExecutionRequest,
    ) -> PublicationExecutionResult:
        if publication is None:
            raise ValueError("publication cannot be None.")

        existing = self._completed.get(request.idempotency_key)
        if existing is not None:
            return PublicationExecutionResult(
                publication_id=existing.publication_id,
                status=PublicationExecutionStatus.IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY,
                idempotency_key=existing.idempotency_key,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                provider_message_id=existing.provider_message_id,
                error_code=existing.error_code,
                error_message=existing.error_message,
            )

        self._assert_approved(publication)
        publication.begin_publish()

        try:
            provider_message_id = await self._publisher.publish(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                title=publication.title,
                content=publication.content,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            error_code = self._error_code(exc)
            publication.mark_failure(error_code)
            await self._audit.record_failure(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                actor=request.actor,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                error_code=error_code,
            )
            result = PublicationExecutionResult(
                publication_id=publication.id,
                status=PublicationExecutionStatus.FAILED,
                idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
                correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
                error_code=error_code,
            )
            return result

        publication.publish_success(provider_message_id)
        await self._audit.record_success(
            publication_id=publication.id,
            actor=request.actor,
            correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )

        result = PublicationExecutionResult(
            publication_id=publication.id,
            status=PublicationExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
            idempotency_key=request.idempotency_key,
            correlation_id=request.correlation_id,
            provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
        )
        self._completed[request.idempotency_key] = result
        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _assert_approved(publication: ExecutablePublication) -> None:
        status_value = getattr(publication.status, "value", publication.status)
        if status_value != "approved":
            raise ValueError(
                "Only approved publications may be executed."
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _error_code(exc: Exception) -> str:
        """Return a stable, non-sensitive operational error code."""
        explicit = getattr(exc, "error_code", None)
        if isinstance(explicit, str) and explicit.strip():
            return explicit.strip()[:100]
        return type(exc).__name__.upper()[:100]

"""WS-22.3.1 provider/channel-independent ports."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

from backend.app.domain.announcement_publication.execution import (
    PublishAnnouncementCommand,
    PublicationExecutionResult,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PublicationForExecution:
    """Minimal execution projection required by the use case.

    The adapter/application layer can map the existing WS-22.1
    publication model into this projection without coupling the execution
    engine to a specific channel provider.
    """

    publication_id: str
    status: str
    destination: str
    rendered_content: str


class PublicationExecutionRepository(Protocol):
    """Port for loading and recording publication execution state."""

    async def get_for_execution(
        self,
        publication_id: str,
    ) -> PublicationForExecution | None:
        ...

    async def record_execution(
        self,
        result: PublicationExecutionResult,
    ) -> None:
        ...


class PublicationPublisher(Protocol):
    """Provider/channel-neutral publishing port."""

    async def publish(
        self,
        *,
        publication: PublicationForExecution,
        idempotency_key: str,
    ) -> str:
        """Publish and return an opaque provider reference.

        Implementations must not expose credentials through the result.
        """
        ...


class PublicationAuditSink(Protocol):
    """Port for durable/observable publication audit events."""

    async def record(self, event: object) -> None:
        ...


class PublicationIdempotencyStore(Protocol):
    """Port preventing duplicate external publication attempts."""

    async def get_result(
        self,
        idempotency_key: str,
    ) -> PublicationExecutionResult | None:
        ...

    async def store_result(
        self,
        result: PublicationExecutionResult,
    ) -> None:
        ...


__all__ = [
    "PublicationAuditSink",
    "PublicationExecutionRepository",
    "PublicationExecutionResult",
    "PublicationForExecution",
    "PublicationIdempotencyStore",
    "PublicationPublisher",
]

"""WS-22.3.1 publication execution application contract."""

from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.application.announcement_operations.publication_execution_ports import (
    PublicationAuditSink,
    PublicationExecutionRepository,
    PublicationIdempotencyStore,
    PublicationPublisher,
)
from backend.app.domain.announcement_publication.execution import (
    PublishAnnouncementCommand,
    PublicationAuditEvent,
    PublicationExecutionErrorCode,
    PublicationExecutionResult,
)


class PublicationExecutionService:
    """Execute an approved publication through an injected publishing port.

    This service contains orchestration only. It does not know Telegram,
    HTTP, frontend concerns, credentials, or provider-specific APIs.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        repository: PublicationExecutionRepository,
        publisher: PublicationPublisher,
        idempotency_store: PublicationIdempotencyStore,
        audit_sink: PublicationAuditSink,
    ) -> None:
        if any(
            dependency is None
            for dependency in (
                repository,
                publisher,
                idempotency_store,
                audit_sink,
            )
        ):
            raise ValueError("All publication execution dependencies are required.")

        self._repository = repository
        self._publisher = publisher
        self._idempotency_store = idempotency_store
        self._audit_sink = audit_sink

    async def execute(
        self,
        command: PublishAnnouncementCommand,
    ) -> PublicationExecutionResult:
        """Execute one explicit publication request."""

        existing = await self._idempotency_store.get_result(
            command.idempotency_key
        )
        if existing is not None:
            return existing

        publication = await self._repository.get_for_execution(
            command.publication_id
        )

        if publication is None:
            result = PublicationExecutionResult.failed(
                publication_id=command.publication_id,
                idempotency_key=command.idempotency_key,
                error_code=PublicationExecutionErrorCode.INVALID_STATE,
                error_message="Publication is not available for execution.",
            )
            await self._record_result(command, result)
            return result

        if publication.status.lower() not in {"approved", "ready_to_publish"}:
            result = PublicationExecutionResult.failed(
                publication_id=command.publication_id,
                idempotency_key=command.idempotency_key,
                error_code=PublicationExecutionErrorCode.INVALID_STATE,
                error_message="Publication is not in an executable state.",
            )
            await self._record_result(command, result)
            return result

        try:
            provider_reference = await self._publisher.publish(
                publication=publication,
                idempotency_key=command.idempotency_key,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            result = PublicationExecutionResult.failed(
                publication_id=command.publication_id,
                idempotency_key=command.idempotency_key,
                error_code=PublicationExecutionErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR,
                error_message=str(exc) or "Publication provider failed.",
            )
            await self._record_result(command, result)
            return result

        result = PublicationExecutionResult.succeeded(
            publication_id=command.publication_id,
            idempotency_key=command.idempotency_key,
            provider_reference=provider_reference,
        )
        await self._record_result(command, result)
        return result

    async def _record_result(
        self,
        command: PublishAnnouncementCommand,
        result: PublicationExecutionResult,
    ) -> None:
        await self._idempotency_store.store_result(result)
        await self._repository.record_execution(result)

        await self._audit_sink.record(
            PublicationAuditEvent(
                event_name="announcement_publication_execution",
                publication_id=result.publication_id,
                requested_by=command.requested_by,
                status=result.status,
                occurred_at=result.executed_at,
                idempotency_key=result.idempotency_key,
                provider_reference=result.provider_reference,
                error_code=result.error_code,
                safe_metadata={"execution_status": result.status.value},
            )
        )


__all__ = ["PublicationExecutionService"]

from __future__ import annotations

from backend.app.domain.authorization.permissions import Permission, has_permission
from backend.app.domain.identity.principal import Principal


class AuthenticationRequiredError(PermissionError):
    """No valid authenticated principal exists."""


class PermissionDeniedError(PermissionError):
    """Authenticated principal lacks a permission."""


class AuthorizationService:
    """Provider-neutral authorization boundary."""

    def require_authenticated(
        self,
        principal: Principal | None,
    ) -> Principal:
        if principal is None or not principal.is_active:
            raise AuthenticationRequiredError(
                "Authenticated application identity is required."
            )
        return principal

    def require_permission(
        self,
        *,
        principal: Principal | None,
        permission: Permission,
    ) -> Principal:
        authenticated = self.require_authenticated(principal)

        if not has_permission(
            roles=authenticated.roles,
            permission=permission,
        ):
            raise PermissionDeniedError(
                f"Permission required: {permission.value}."
            )

        return authenticated

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import logging
import secrets

from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Iterator

from .models import (
    BetaConnectionToken,
    BetaUserState,
    TelegramBinding,
)

from .repositories import (
    BetaTokenRepository,
    BetaUserRepository,
    TelegramBindingRepository,
)


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BetaConnectionTokenResult:
    token: str
    connection: BetaConnectionToken

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[object]:
        yield self.token
        yield self.connection


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BetaConversationContext:
    user_id: str
    telegram_user_id: int
    email: str
    world_id: str
    character: str
    level: str


class BetaAccessService:
    """
    Application boundary for Beta eligibility,
    Telegram binding and authorization.

    Telegram identity invariant:

        One Telegram identity
        -> one Beta account

    A Telegram identity that is already connected cannot
    be rebound to another Beta account through a new
    connection token.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        user_repository: BetaUserRepository,
        token_repository: BetaTokenRepository,
        binding_repository: TelegramBindingRepository,
        expiration_minutes: int = 1440,
    ) -> None:
        if expiration_minutes <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "expiration_minutes must be positive."
            )

        self._users = user_repository
        self._tokens = token_repository
        self._bindings = binding_repository
        self._expiration_minutes = expiration_minutes

    async def approve_beta(
        self,
        user_id: str,
    ) -> BetaUserState:
        user = await self._require_user(user_id)

        if not user.email_verified:
            raise ValueError(
                "Email must be verified before Beta approval."
            )

        return await self._users.save(
            replace(
                user,
                beta_approved=True,
            )
        )

    async def assign_world(
        self,
        *,
        user_id: str,
        world_id: str,
    ) -> BetaUserState:
        if not world_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "world_id is required."
            )

        user = await self._require_user(user_id)

        if not user.email_verified:
            raise ValueError(
                "Email must be verified before World assignment."
            )

        if not user.beta_approved:
            raise ValueError(
                "User is not Beta approved."
            )

        return await self._users.save(
            replace(
                user,
                active_world_id=world_id,
            )
        )

    async def create_connection_token(
        self,
        user_id: str,
    ) -> BetaConnectionTokenResult:
        user = await self._require_user(user_id)

        if not user.email_verified:
            raise ValueError(
                "Email is not verified."
            )

        if not user.beta_approved:
            raise ValueError(
                "User is not Beta approved."
            )

        if not user.active_world_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "User must have a Learning World before Telegram access."
            )

        raw_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)

        token = BetaConnectionToken(
            token_id=secrets.token_hex(16),
            user_id=user.user_id,
            token_hash=self.hash_token(
                raw_token
            ),
            expires_at=(
                datetime.now(timezone.utc)
                + timedelta(
                    minutes=self._expiration_minutes
                )
            ),
        )

        await self._tokens.save(token)

        return BetaConnectionTokenResult(
            token=raw_token,
            connection=token,
        )

    async def validate_and_bind(
        self,
        *,
        token: str,
        telegram_id: int,
        chat_id: int,
    ) -> BetaUserState:
        record = await self._tokens.get_by_hash(
            self.hash_token(token)
        )

        if record is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Invalid connection token."
            )

        if record.used:
            raise ValueError(
                "Connection token already used."
            )

        expires_at = record.expires_at

        if expires_at.tzinfo is None:
            expires_at = expires_at.replace(
                tzinfo=timezone.utc
            )

        if expires_at <= datetime.now(timezone.utc):
            raise ValueError(
                "Connection token expired."
            )

        user = await self._require_user(
            record.user_id
        )

        if not user.eligible:
            raise ValueError(
                "User is not eligible."
            )

        # -------------------------------------------------
        # Telegram identity ownership invariant
        #
        # A Telegram identity may belong to only one
        # Beta account. Never silently transfer ownership.
        # -------------------------------------------------

        existing_binding = (
            await self._bindings.get_by_telegram_user_id(
                str(telegram_id)
            )
        )

        if existing_binding is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram identity is already connected."
            )

        await self._bindings.save(
            TelegramBinding(
                binding_id=secrets.token_hex(16),
                user_id=user.user_id,
                telegram_user_id=str(
                    telegram_id
                ),
                chat_id=str(
                    chat_id
                ),
                connected_at=datetime.now(
                    timezone.utc
                ),
            )
        )

        await self._tokens.mark_used(
            replace(
                record,
                used_at=datetime.now(
                    timezone.utc
                ),
            )
        )

        return await self._users.save(
            replace(
                user,
                telegram_id=telegram_id,
            )
        )

    async def authorize_private_chat(
        self,
        telegram_id: int,
    ) -> BetaUserState:
        user = await self._users.get_by_telegram_id(
            telegram_id
        )

        if user is None:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Telegram account is not connected."
            )

        if not user.active:
            raise PermissionError(
                "User is not active."
            )

        return user

    async def get_conversation_context(
        self,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> BetaConversationContext:
        user = await self.authorize_private_chat(
            telegram_user_id
        )

        return BetaConversationContext(
            user_id=user.user_id,
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            email=user.email,
            world_id=(
                user.active_world_id
                or "world-fr"
            ),
            character="Alix",
            level="B1",
        )

    @staticmethod
    def hash_token(
        token: str,
    ) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(
            token.encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()

    async def _require_user(
        self,
        user_id: str,
    ) -> BetaUserState:
        user = await self._users.get(
            user_id
        )

        if user is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Academy user does not exist."
            )

        return user

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any, Protocol

from backend.app.application.beta_access.beta_access_service import (
    BetaAccessService,
)
from backend.app.application.beta_access.policies.telegram_policy_messages import (
    TelegramPolicyMessageService,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TelegramPolicy(Protocol):
    async def allow(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> bool:
        ...


class TelegramObservability(Protocol):
    async def record(
        self,
        *,
        event_type: str,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        outcome: str,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        ...


class BetaTelegramConversationBoundary:
    """Application policy boundary for Beta Telegram conversations.

    Security / resilience order:

        Telegram identity
              â†“
        Message validation
              â†“
        Beta authorization / context
              â†“
        Rate limit
              â†“
        Abuse protection
              â†“
        Conversation service
              â†“
        Observability
              â†“
        Safe response

    Rate limiting and abuse protection deliberately remain outside
    TelegramConversationService and outside Telegram transport.

    Dependency failures are contained at this application boundary so
    infrastructure/provider exceptions never become learner-facing Telegram
    responses.
    """

    MAX_TELEGRAM_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 4096

    SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, something went wrong while processing your message. "
        "Please try again later."
    )

    UNAUTHORIZED_RESPONSE = (
        "Sorry, this Telegram account is not authorized "
        "and is not approved for Beta access."
    )

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        conversation_service: Any,
        beta_access_service: BetaAccessService,
        rate_limiter: TelegramPolicy | None = None,
        abuse_protector: TelegramPolicy | None = None,
        observability: TelegramObservability | None = None,
        policy_message_service: TelegramPolicyMessageService | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if conversation_service is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "conversation_service cannot be None."
            )

        if beta_access_service is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "beta_access_service cannot be None."
            )

        self._conversation_service = conversation_service
        self._beta_access_service = beta_access_service
        self._rate_limiter = rate_limiter
        self._abuse_protector = abuse_protector
        self._observability = observability
        self._policy_message_service = (
            policy_message_service
            or TelegramPolicyMessageService()
        )

    async def _record(
        self,
        *,
        event_type: str,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        outcome: str,
        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if self._observability is None:
            return

        try:
            await self._observability.record(
                event_type=event_type,
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome=outcome,
                metadata=metadata,
            )
        except Exception:
            # Observability must never break classroom processing.
            logger.exception(
                "Telegram observability failure for event_type=%s.",
                event_type,
            )

    async def handle_message(
        self,
        *,
        telegram_user_id: int,
        message: str,
    ) -> Any:
        self._validate_telegram_user_id(
            telegram_user_id,
        )

        clean_message = self._validate_message(
            message,
        )

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Beta authorization / World context
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        try:
            context = await (
                self._beta_access_service
                .get_conversation_context(
                    telegram_user_id,
                )
            )

        except PermissionError:
            await self._record(
                event_type="telegram_classroom_authorization",
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome="denied",
            )

            return self.UNAUTHORIZED_RESPONSE

        except Exception as exc:
            # Infrastructure failures such as PostgreSQL outages must not
            # escape to Telegram. Log only the exception type here; the
            # learner must never receive internal dependency details.
            await self._record(
                event_type="telegram_classroom_authorization",
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome="error",
                metadata={
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                },
            )

            logger.exception(
                "Telegram Beta access/context resolution failed."
            )

            return self.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Rate limiting
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        if self._rate_limiter is not None:
            try:
                allowed = await self._rate_limiter.allow(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                )

            except Exception as exc:
                await self._record(
                    event_type="telegram_classroom_rate_limit",
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    outcome="error",
                    metadata={
                        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    },
                )

                logger.exception(
                    "Telegram rate limiter failed."
                )

                return self.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE

            if not allowed:
                await self._record(
                    event_type="telegram_classroom_rate_limit",
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    outcome="blocked",
                    metadata={
                        "world_id": context.world_id,
                    },
                )

                return (
                    self._policy_message_service
                    .rate_limit_message(
                        context=context,
                        retry_after_seconds=(
                            self._get_rate_limit_retry_after_seconds()
                        ),
                    )
                )

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Abuse protection
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        if self._abuse_protector is not None:
            try:
                allowed = await self._abuse_protector.allow(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                )

            except Exception as exc:
                await self._record(
                    event_type=(
                        "telegram_classroom_abuse_protection"
                    ),
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    outcome="error",
                    metadata={
                        "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    },
                )

                logger.exception(
                    "Telegram abuse protection failed."
                )

                return self.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE

            if not allowed:
                await self._record(
                    event_type=(
                        "telegram_classroom_abuse_protection"
                    ),
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    outcome="blocked",
                    metadata={
                        "world_id": context.world_id,
                    },
                )

                return (
                    self._policy_message_service
                    .abuse_protection_message(
                        context=context,
                        retry_after_seconds=(
                            self._get_abuse_retry_after_seconds()
                        ),
                    )
                )

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Accepted classroom message
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        await self._record(
            event_type="telegram_classroom_message",
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            outcome="accepted",
            metadata={
                "world_id": context.world_id,
                "character": context.character,
                "level": context.level,
            },
        )

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Conversation / AI Runtime
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        try:
            context_handler = getattr(
                self._conversation_service,
                "handle_telegram_message_with_context",
                None,
            )

            if context_handler is not None:
                response = await context_handler(
                    telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                    message=clean_message,
                    context=context,
                )

            else:
                response = await (
                    self._conversation_service
                    .handle_telegram_message(
                        telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                        message=clean_message,
                    )
                )

        except Exception as exc:
            await self._record(
                event_type="telegram_classroom_conversation",
                telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
                outcome="error",
                metadata={
                    "world_id": context.world_id,
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                },
            )

            logger.exception(
                "Telegram conversation processing failed."
            )

            return self.SAFE_ERROR_RESPONSE

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Successful completion
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        await self._record(
            event_type="telegram_classroom_conversation",
            telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id,
            outcome="success",
            metadata={
                "world_id": context.world_id,
                "character": context.character,
                "level": context.level,
            },
        )

        return response

    def _get_rate_limit_retry_after_seconds(self) -> int:
        """Return the configured rate-limit retry period.

        The policy message service is responsible for learner-facing
        language. This method deliberately avoids exposing implementation
        internals.
        """

        limiter = self._rate_limiter

        if limiter is None:
            return 60

        window = getattr(
            limiter,
            "window_seconds",
            60,
        )

        try:
            return max(
                1,
                int(float(window)),
            )
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 60

    def _get_abuse_retry_after_seconds(self) -> int:
        """Return the configured abuse-protection retry period."""

        protector = self._abuse_protector

        if protector is None:
            return 60

        window = getattr(
            protector,
            "window_seconds",
            60,
        )

        try:
            return max(
                1,
                int(float(window)),
            )
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return 60

    @classmethod
    def _validate_telegram_user_id(
        cls,
        telegram_user_id: int,
    ) -> None:
        if isinstance(telegram_user_id, bool):
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

        if not isinstance(
            telegram_user_id,
            int,
        ):
            raise TypeError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

        if telegram_user_id <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram user ID must be a positive integer."
            )

    @classmethod
    def _validate_message(
        cls,
        message: str,
    ) -> str:
        if message is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message cannot be empty."
            )

        if not isinstance(
            message,
            str,
        ):
            raise TypeError(
                "Telegram message must be a string."
            )

        if not message or not message.strip():
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message cannot be empty."
            )

        clean_message = message.strip()

        if len(clean_message) > cls.MAX_TELEGRAM_MESSAGE_LENGTH:
            raise ValueError(
                "Telegram message is too long. "
                "Maximum length is "
                f"{cls.MAX_TELEGRAM_MESSAGE_LENGTH} characters."
            )

        return clean_message


__all__ = [
    "BetaTelegramConversationBoundary",
]

class BetaTelegramInvitationService:
    """Creates the one-time Telegram deep link and sends the invitation email."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        beta_access_service: BetaAccessService,
        email_sender: BetaEmailSender,
        telegram_bot_username: str,
    ) -> None:
        if not telegram_bot_username:
            raise ValueError("telegram_bot_username is required.")
        self._access = beta_access_service
        self._email_sender = email_sender
        self._bot_username = telegram_bot_username.lstrip("@")

    async def send_invitation(self, *, user_id: str) -> str:
        raw_token, _ = await self._access.create_connection_token(user_id)
        classroom_url = (
            f"https://t.me/{self._bot_username}?start={raw_token}"
        )

        user = await self._access._require_user(user_id)
        await self._email_sender.send_beta_invitation(
            email=user.email,
            classroom_url=classroom_url,
        )
        return classroom_url

class BetaAccessStatus(StrEnum):
    """
    Beta access lifecycle states.
    """

    PENDING_VERIFICATION = "PENDING_VERIFICATION"
    PENDING_APPROVAL = "PENDING_APPROVAL"
    ELIGIBLE = "ELIGIBLE"
    TELEGRAM_CONNECTED = "TELEGRAM_CONNECTED"
    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    DENIED = "DENIED"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BetaUserState:
    """
    Domain model representing a Beta user.

    Identity flow:

        beta_users
             |
             v
        telegram_bindings
             |
             v
        Telegram private chat
    """

    user_id: str

    email: str

    email_verified: bool

    beta_approved: bool

    telegram_id: int | None = None

    active_world_id: str | None = None


    @property
    def eligible(self) -> bool:
        """
        User can access Beta if approved and verified.
        """

        return (
            self.email_verified
            and self.beta_approved
        )


    @property
    def active(self) -> bool:
        """
        User can enter private Telegram classroom.
        """

        return (
            self.eligible
            and self.telegram_id is not None
            and self.active_world_id is not None
        )
